quest.title: Presumption of Innocence
quest.description: Sister Victoria seems to be thinking about something...

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: I wonder if he will finally repent this time...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Repent from what?

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: Lots of people come here every day to confess their sins and seek forgiveness from the gods.

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: But if you only say it and don't act on it, don't you think that's a waste of time?

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: Take Nimrod for instance. He has come here to confess his alcohol abuse numerous times, but he hasn't changed one bit...

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: If you have time, maybe you could go and check up on him?

response.speaker: Victoria
response.text: Oh — and if he is drinking again, please bring some evidence back.

response.speaker: Victoria
response.text: Sometimes, serial offenders need a little instruction to help them correct the error of their ways...

response.speaker: Victoria
response.text: Drinking alone is not a sin. But it is sinful to drink to the point that you bring undue distress to others.

response.speaker: Victoria
response.text: If everyone was to behave quite so unscrupulously, sooner or later the entirety of Mondstadt would find itself in a very distressing situation.

response.speaker: Victoria
response.text: So each time a sin rears its ugly head, it needs to be nipped in the bud. Now, quickly, go check up on Nimrod for me.

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: Hahaha, this is the one I look forward to every day...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I thought you quit drinking?

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: Argh! Oh, you gave me a fright... I thought it was my wife.

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: The odd one now and then doesn't hurt anybody! I did have a tough day's work today...

dialogues.speaker: Nimrod
dialogues.text: Alright, I get it! I'll finish off this one and head back. Eury will probably have finished shopping by now anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: Hello? Can I help?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Tell me about Nimrod.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: He's been here drinking for hours. Look, here's his tab.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: If he keeps this up, we'll have to call in Eury.

dialogues.speaker: Charles
dialogues.text: You want to borrow it? I suppose there's no harm in that — but what do you need it for?

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: Have you checked up on him yet?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is Nimrod's bill from the tavern.

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: Hmph. Just as I thought, he's at it again.

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: People will forget everything that's happened in their past unless they've really had to suffer for it...

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: Please take this as payment for your trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: As for Nimrod's payback... I will mull it over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *Tut-tut* Simply no attempt to change his ways whatsoever...

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: People don't tend to learn the lessons that their past can teach them unless... Unless somebody points it out to them directly.

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: Have you checked up on him yet?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Nimrod is sober as a judge.

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: ...Really? He's sober?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Unfortunately there's no evidence...

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: That's okay. So long as you found no evidence of him drinking, I am content to believe he is a changed man.

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: Until I am given evidence to the contrary, I am always willing to believe in a person's innocence.

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: But when there's mountains of evidence telling of all kinds of misdemeanors... It really is funny.

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: Please take this to pay you back for your trouble. I hope I don't see the day that you have anything to repent for.

dialogues.speaker: Victoria
dialogues.text: People don't tend to learn the lessons that their past can teach them unless... Unless somebody points it out to them directly.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: I've had no end of customers again today, I'm beat...
